figures.caption: Figure 2 Illustration of the schedule completion flow network. The left part shows the graph ŜE(G, D), obtained from the static expansion SE(G, D) by adding a global source s and sink z. Its edges consist of demand edges (solid, blue), waiting edges (dashed, orange), filler edges (solid, gray), and the edges incident with s and z (solid, black). The flow ranges are indicated in the two layers on the bottom right and also by the edge colors: orange and black edges have range (0, ∞), blue edges have range (1, 1), and gray edges have range (0, 1).
Figure 10 Example instance with n = 5 vertices, which gives h = 6. Numbers next to edges indicate a demand at that time. A possible solution for the EDP instance consists of the paths {ade, ac, bce}.

Figure 8 Illustration of the gap compression step. The left part shows some layers of a flow network with a large gap between the relevant time steps t1 and t2. The right part shows the replacement of these layers by a single compressed layer connecting all vertices from the (t1 + 1)-th layer to all reachable vertices from the t2-th layer.

Figure 1 Illustration of the schedule completion problem. Depicted on the top right are the underlying static graph G and the demand edges of the draft schedule D. On the left is the static expansion SE(G, D) with the demand edges highlighted in blue. At the bottom right, we see three different schedules extending D: the unconstrained schedule consisting of p1 = (a, d, c, d, a) and p2 = (a, b, c, b); the length-constrained schedule p1 = (a, d, c, b), p2 = (c, d, c, a), and p3 = (a, b); and the lifespan-constrained schedule p1 = (a, d, c), p2 = (c, d, c, a), p3 = (a, b), and p4 = (c, b); both under the restriction h = 3.
